# SBFB workflow agents — agent index

> Deterministic multi-agent workflows executed by a host-side Rust runtime:
> signed portable packs (`SBFBPromptAgentPack.v1`), an authoritative compiler
> (`CompiledPlan.v1`), and a durable SQLite run store. This index points an
> agent at the rank-1 sources for the parts DELIVERED so far — it is seeded at
> **S83 Phase I1** with the run store loopback read family and grows with each
> phase; the chantier-wide closure (full GUIDE + every contract) is the S83
> wrap-up (Phase AJ1).
>
> **Status: UNDER CONSTRUCTION (S83).** Delivered at this seed: pack format
> (F), language + agent definitions (G), compiler (H), durable run store (I),
> run store loopback READ surface (I1), deterministic orchestrator (J),
> effect layer — activities, retries, idempotence, outcome_unknown (K),
> effective-capability COMPUTATION — 7-layer monotone intersection, 17 typed
> classes (L), host secret vault + HITL binding/signature PRIMITIVES and the
> host-chrome approval affordance (L1). The per-effect BINDING of L/L1 into
> dispatch (**0 call-site today** for the vault, the secret seam, the binding
> and the host signer), adapters (N/O) and the Workflow Hub app are later
> phases — a fact about them absent from a rank-1 repo file is
> **`Not evidenced`**.
>
> **Truth Stack** (trust the higher rank on conflict):
> `repo files > .planning/active/ > commits > prompts > chat`.

## Start here

- [WORKFLOW_AGENTS_OVERVIEW.md](../factory/WORKFLOW_AGENTS_OVERVIEW.md): the
  chantier GUIDE (4 authority layers, invariants, phase map). Grows each
  phase; finalized at AJ1.
- [REFERENCE.md](./REFERENCE.md): human twin of this index — the run store
  loopback API family (envelopes, tiers, invariants).

## Run store loopback surface (rank-1 source, S83 Phase I1)

- [workflow_api.rs](../../crates/nexus-shell-daemon/src/workflow_api.rs): the 2
  `/api/daemon/workflow/*` route handlers (READ-ONLY family; routes stay
  registered in `http.rs` `build_router`/`authed_routes` — loopback bearer +
  Host + Origin, peer creds at the listener). Aggregate per-run projection
  `crates/nexus-shell-daemon/src/workflow_api.rs:workflow_run_response`
  (scalar allowlist — never a raw `RunEvent`, snapshot or effect receipt) +
  raw lease row `crates/nexus-shell-daemon/src/workflow_api.rs:workflow_lease_response`.
  `run_id` is server-validated at the route
  (`crates/nexus-shell-daemon/src/workflow_api.rs:valid_run_id`, bounded
  charset, 400 on violation; a run_id never forms a filesystem path).
- [store.rs](../../crates/sbfb-workflow-engine/src/store.rs): the durable run
  store the routes read (journal + outbox + inbox + snapshots + lease;
  single-writer epoch-CAS fencing; forward-only migrations, downgrade guard
  at open). The daemon holds ONE boot-opened handle and acquires NO lease at
  I1 — reads are unfenced-safe under WAL; the write path is the Phase J
  runtime.
- [run_event.rs](../../crates/sbfb-workflow-core/src/run_event.rs): the
  `RunEvent.v1` envelope (LOCAL store format, `RUN_EVENT_FORMAT_VERSION`
  never a wire version; `DOMAIN_RUN_EVENT_V1` stays RESERVED 0-producer).
- [LOOPBACK_ENDPOINTS_TRUST_TIERS.md](../security/LOOPBACK_ENDPOINTS_TRUST_TIERS.md):
  D7 inventory §3 — the T0 representative row for this family, plus the 3
  MUTATING endpoints (restore / gc / lease-force) tier-classified **T1,
  re-routed to Phase V** (the "Centre des Runs" operator surface) by Phase K
  (they do NOT exist in the router today; K is engine-only).
- [THREAT_MODEL.md](../security/THREAT_MODEL.md): §19 asset A11 + the
  T-RUN-* rows, plus §19.2 (asset A12) — the effect layer's own threats
  (v26 = the Phase K effect surface), plus §19.3 (asset A13) — the
  permissions surface (v27 = the Phase L capability computation), plus **§19.4
  (assets A14 + A15)** — the secret vault and the signed host HITL approval
  (v28 = Phase L1). Read its DS-1 paragraph first: every row whose enforcement
  depends on the un-built wiring is **`bornee`**, never `fermee`.

## Permissions surface (rank-1 source, S83 Phase L)

- [capability.rs](../../crates/sbfb-workflow-engine/src/capability.rs): the
  authoritative `effective_capabilities` computation — the monotone
  intersection of the seven authority layers (§14.1) over 17 typed capability
  classes (§14.2). PURE: no I/O, no serde derive (nothing serialized —
  census DOMAIN 29 untouched), the OS toggle and local policy come from an
  injected `CapabilityPolicy` trait. Each present layer can only ATTENUATE;
  meet is field-by-field with per-field direction (min quota/timeout,
  intersect destinations, MAX approval, UNION of the `DataPolicy` flags —
  never a total max that would drop an orthogonal axis). Multiple same-
  audience grants for a ref reduce to the DOMINATING grant (the one every
  other refines) if it exists, else a fail-closed drop — permutation-
  invariant, never a synthesised field-wise LUB. Mirrors — never calls —
  `sbfb-manifest::grant_v0` (wrong domain: the 16 bridge verbs). The
  per-effect BINDING into dispatch and the authority-refusal journal are the
  run-surface phase (DS-1); the secret vault and signed HITL are L1 (the
  layer-7 decision here is an OPAQUE ref, empty in L, fail-closed on `Human`).
  L1 narrowed this API: `HitlValidity::decided_refs` is now PRIVATE and
  `DecidedRef` — minted only by `decide_ref` — is its sole producer, so the
  "build the authority set from the PENDING queue" bypass no longer compiles
  from another crate.

## Secret vault + host HITL surface (rank-1 source, S83 Phase L1)

**0 call-site of production** for everything in this section (DS-1): these are
PRIMITIVES plus a host-chrome affordance, not a wired path. Nothing crosses the
boundary yet, which is why §4/§5/§6 of the threat model are deliberately
unchanged — drawing a shell→daemon data flow today would be a PROMISE, and this
repo does not write promises into rank-1 files. The honest bounds (numbered)
are §19.4 of [THREAT_MODEL.md](../security/THREAT_MODEL.md). No count is given
here on purpose: the list grows, and a count no gate recounts is exactly the
class of claim this repo keeps getting wrong.

- [vault.rs](../../crates/nexus-core-rs/src/vault.rs): the HOST secret vault.
  Named secrets sealed AT REST, bound to their opaque ref JUST-BEFORE the call.
  Reuses the Sprint 20 keystore crypto — Argon2id(PIN) → KEK, AES-256-GCM,
  `DOMAIN_KEYSTORE_V1` as the shared domain (sub-context `secret-vault`, NOT a
  new `DOMAIN_*_V1`) — so the census stays at 29 and no wire format moves. The
  at-rest defense that actually exists is Argon2id(PIN): the OS keyring layer is
  INERT in this workspace (mock builder), stated in the module rather than
  claimed. The FOUR writing/binding entry points — `bind`, `put`, `rotate`,
  `delete` — re-read the on-disk epoch and fail closed
  (`ConcurrentModification`) rather than answering from a stale snapshot —
  EXCEPT after the lost-update collision of **bound 27 of §19.4** — ONE of the
  states, not the only one — where a handle holds the DISK's epoch over a
  stale BODY. There the
  re-read passes and all FOUR answer from that stale body: `bind` serves a
  revoked entry, `delete` returns `Ok(false)` and `rotate` returns
  `UnknownRef` — both meaning only "my copy did not have it" — and `put`
  COMMITS the stale body, silently undoing the other handle's write. Read the
  guarantee as "re-reads the epoch", never as "never answers from a stale
  snapshot". A SECOND, ordinary window needs no collision at all: the epoch
  check and the body read are not atomic, so a bind admitted at epoch `n` can
  complete after another handle commits a `delete` at `n+1`. That execution is
  linearisable — the bind is admitted at the check — so state it as semantics,
  not as a bug: **a bind admitted before a revocation may complete, and be
  USED, after it** (even a bind that finishes first hands a `VaultSecret` the
  provider consumes later);
  `refs()`, `inventory()` and `epoch()` answer from THIS HANDLE'S snapshot and
  are never a proof of what is committed.
- [secret.rs](../../crates/sbfb-workflow-engine/src/secret.rs): the ENGINE side
  of the seam. The engine only ever knows the opaque `SecretRef`; `BoundSecret`
  has NO `Serialize` (a compile-time fact, not a review rule), a redacting
  `Debug`, and zeroises on drop.
- [hitl.rs](../../crates/sbfb-workflow-engine/src/hitl.rs): the KEYLESS binding.
  `hitl_binding_digest` over the EXACT 15-field tuple; `verify_binding` refuses
  any mutation and any expired approval. Pure — the engine holds no key.
- [hitl_approval.rs](../../crates/nexus-core-rs/src/hitl_approval.rs): the HOST
  AUTHORITY. The daemon — sole holder of the unlocked node identity — signs the
  binding digest under a LOCAL context (`sbfb-hitl-approval-v1`, not a
  `DOMAIN_*_V1` family: consumed on ONE node, before ONE effect, never gossiped).
- [Approvals.tsx](../../web/src/pages/Approvals.tsx) + [approvalsQueue.ts](../../web/src/pages/approvalsQueue.ts):
  the host-chrome affordance at `/approvals`. Renders the exact tuple (WYSIWYS),
  holds NO key and does NO crypto, and owns the queue in the HOST document so it
  survives an iframe dying. Who renders and who signs are different layers: the
  browser shell renders (0 key), the daemon signs.

## Contract tests (drift gates)

- `golden_http_workflow_domain` + `golden_families_stable` probes in
  [test_support.rs](../../crates/nexus-shell-daemon/src/test_support.rs):
  the EMPTY-NODE contract of both routes, replayed against two fresh nodes.
- In-module tests in `workflow_api.rs`: projection allowlist key-set pin,
  duress-identical behaviour, bounded `run_id` guard.
